analysis: The PR adds `.github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml`, a dispatch-only lane. `build-sign` (macOS, no secrets) builds an arbitrary ref and ad-hoc signs it (lines 59-209). `publish` (Ubuntu) holds DEV_RELEASE_KEY and the dev R2 keys, and registers the bundle on the dev coordinator (lines 211-295). The changelog and docs/developer/test.md describe an installer relaxation, but `scripts/install.sh` and `scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py` are not in this batch, so their coverage is unexamined. The changelog says the installer accepts ad-hoc or non-Apple-anchored signatures for versions containing `-dev.` or `-staging.`. Whether that check relies on the version string alone is a cross-file question for the next pass. Related threats: TB-009, T-034, T-013, T-054 (self-reported hashes and cdhash qualification), A-011 and A-017. Trust gaps noted: build-job outputs flow unvalidated into the credentialed job (line 221), and nothing pins execution to the master workflow definition (line 42). Unreviewed items: whether `scripts/provider-release-publication.py prepare` re-verifies hashes, version and provenance; whether the ad-hoc cdhash can reach App Attest durable qualification (A-017); and whether the production-served installer also accepts ad-hoc signatures for `-dev.` versions, which could widen downgrade risk if release metadata is tampered with. This pass saw no installer diff and no tests, so needs_deeper_review is true.

findings.detail: The `build-sign` job runs arbitrary branch code: the checked-out composite action, `scripts/check-release-version.sh`, `provider-signing-validation.py` and `Package.swift`. Its outputs (`version`, `source_sha`, `binary_hash`, `bundle_hash`, `metallib_hash`, `code_directory_hash`) are passed unvalidated into the `publish` job's env. `publish` holds `DEV_RELEASE_KEY` and the dev R2 keys. The workflow does not re-check that `VERSION` matches `X.Y.Z-dev.branch.N`, recompute the hashes from the downloaded bundle, or confirm that `RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA` is the commit that was built. A malicious branch can therefore emit a forged version, a master SHA as source provenance, or hashes that differ from the bundle. The master `prepare` script may reject some of these, but that is not visible here. The result is a blessed-hash registration (A-011) on the dev coordinator with spoofed provenance, and a version string that can steer the installer's relaxed ad-hoc signature path. Fix: in `publish`, validate the version with a strict regex, recompute every hash from the downloaded tarball, and derive the source SHA from the trusted run context (not from job output) before any credentialed step.
findings.title: Publish job trusts identity values emitted by the untrusted branch-build job

findings.detail: The header says the file is dispatched on master and that the credentialed `publish` logic is the reviewed master copy. Nothing enforces this. `workflow_dispatch` executes the workflow definition from whichever ref is selected. A collaborator with write access can dispatch a branch whose copy of this file has an altered `publish` job. That job can read `DEV_RELEASE_KEY`, the dev R2 keys and the dev coordinator URL, because they are repo-level secrets with no protected environment. The master-checkout of the scripts does not prevent this. The result is theft or abuse of the dev release credentials (A-005), and registration of arbitrary binary hashes in the dev blessed-hash registry (A-011). Fix: add `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'` on both jobs, or use a protected environment with required reviewers, and restrict branch-ref dispatch.
findings.title: Credentialed dev-publish workflow has no guard that it runs from the reviewed master definition

findings.detail: `pip install awscli` is unpinned and unhashed. The tool then runs in steps that hold `DEV_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `DEV_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `DEV_RELEASE_KEY`. A compromised or typosquatted package release would execute with those secrets. Fix: pin the version with hashes, or use a preinstalled or checksum-verified CLI.
findings.title: Unpinned awscli installed immediately before steps that hold R2 and release credentials
